test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-II (Held On: 08 Jan, 2024)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank No. 4.
solution:
The correct answer is '**visitors**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage discusses the number of people who come to see the Statue of Unity.
 
• The correct noun should describe individuals who come to view or tour the monument.
 
• "**Visitors**" is the most appropriate term as it refers to people who visit a place for interest, pleasure, or tourism.
 
• Other options ("**guests**", "**invitees**", "**callers**") do not specifically denote tourists or sightseers.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Passage: *The Statue of Unity, a towering tribute to India's Iron Man, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, situated__ on the banks of the majestic Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat's Kevadia, has __witnessed__ a remarkable surge in its annual footfall. In less than five years __since__ its inauguration, this colossal monument has welcomed nearly 16 crore __visitors__. In the first two months after the monument's inauguration in 2018, the world's tallest statue witnessed a whopping 453,020 visitors followed by over 2.7 crore visitors in 2019. Even in 2020, the year tourism sector was battered by a once-in-a-century pandemic and subsequent movement restrictions, nearly 1.3 crore tourists flocked to the Statue of Unity. While the country was still recovering from the Covid-19 pandemic, the Statue of Unity saw a footfall of over 3.4 crores.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Guests: "Guests" typically refers to people who are hosted for social reasons or events, but not specifically for tourism purposes.
 
• Invitees: "Invitees" refers to people who are invited to an event or occasion, which is not suitable for general tourism.
 
• Callers: "Callers" refers to people who make a short visit or phone call; it is not appropriate for the context of tourists and sightseers.
